# ElevenLabs docs: watermarking and the Audio Detector

- Origin: ElevenLabs, "Audio detector" <https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-creative/audio-tools/audio-detector>
  and the help-centre entries "What is watermarking, and why is ElevenLabs using it?",
  "Can I hear the watermark?" and "Is content generated by third-party models available through
  ElevenLabs watermarked?" under <https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/legal/audio-detector/>
  (all read as Markdown via `Accept: text/markdown`)
- Evidence kind: official documentation / official policy FAQ
- Publication date: not stated on any of the pages. Capture date 2026-10-26
- Relevant models: all ElevenLabs-generated speech, including `eleven_v4`; explicitly **not**
  third-party models served through ElevenLabs

## Captured content (verbatim)

### What the watermark is

> Watermarking is a digital technology designed to identify AI-generated content. It embeds
> imperceptible patterns into audio at frequencies masked by existing sound, making the watermark
> completely inaudible while maintaining audio quality.

> ElevenLabs embeds watermarks into audio we generate to make it easier for anyone to verify whether
> a piece of audio originated from our platform.

### Audibility, quality and latency

> No. The watermark is completely inaudible. It hides a pattern of sound at frequencies that are
> masked by the existing audio, making it imperceptible to the human ear.

> Watermarking does not affect audio quality and adds zero latency in nearly all cases.

### Who can detect it

> The Audio Detector can only detect watermarks embedded by ElevenLabs. It will not detect watermarks
> from other AI platforms.

> No other platforms can currently detect ElevenLabs watermarks. Watermarking is focused on public AI
> transparency and is not connected to other platforms' monetization or content policies.

Detection is free for signed-in users; the legacy AI Speech Classifier remains available without
sign-in and "is statistical and may produce false positives or miss modified audio".

### Third-party models are excluded

> Content generated by third-party models available through ElevenLabs is generally not watermarked
> unless explicitly stated otherwise. Watermarking is specific to audio generated directly by
> ElevenLabs models.

## What this establishes

- ElevenLabs watermarks the audio its own models generate, by default, and publishes a detector for
  it. There is **no documented opt-out** for API text-to-speech output on any page captured here, and
  no `watermark` request parameter appears in the Text to Speech or Text to Dialogue API references.
- The watermark is inaudible and, per the vendor, free of quality and latency cost.
- Detection is first-party only: no third-party platform can currently read the mark. So the
  watermark is a transparency/provenance signal for ElevenLabs' own detector, not an
  industry-verifiable provenance standard.
- The exclusion for third-party models is about models hosted *by* ElevenLabs, not about ElevenLabs
  models hosted elsewhere.

## Gaps

- **Whether the watermark survives when `eleven_v4` is served by a reseller host (fal, WaveSpeed) is
  not stated anywhere captured.** Both hosts proxy to the ElevenLabs partner API, so the mark should
  be present, but no source says so and this knowledge base did not test it.
- No statement of what the mark encodes (model ID? workspace? timestamp?) or how robust it is to
  re-encoding, trimming or resampling.
- No statement of whether `eleven_v4_turbo` realtime/WebSocket output is watermarked.
- No regulatory or disclosure obligation is stated beyond "people should know when they are
  interacting with AI-generated content".
